problemStatement.formal: r_3(N) = \max\{|A| : A \subseteq [N],\ A \text{ contains no 3-term arithmetic progression}\} = o(N).
problemStatement.plain: Roth's theorem says that any "dense enough" subset of the integers must contain a 3-term arithmetic progression (three equally spaced numbers like 3, 7, 11). No matter how cleverly you try to avoid creating such patterns, if your set occupies a positive fraction of {1, 2, ..., N}, a 3-term AP will appear once N is large enough. This is the k=3 case of Szemeredi's theorem.

The N=1 sorry is fundamentally about prime N, not just N=1. For prime N, gcd(val(r), N)=1 for all r≠0, so coset decomposition always gives M=1. The density iteration chain breaks when the formal density d_k exceeds 1 while M stays at 1.

Fix options: (a) reduce to N=3^k where M≥3 always, (b) use Bohr sets instead of cosets, (c) restructure chain to short-circuit when d_k > 1 at M=1 (requires proving False from APFree bound in the enclosing context).
N=1 sorry analysis: for d=1, N=1, density_increment_lemma needs |B|≥1.01*M which is impossible (|B|≤M for any B⊆ZMod M). No valid witness exists.
Adding 2≤N hypothesis does NOT fix the issue: the iteration can produce M=1 when N is prime (gcd(val(r),N)=1 for coprime r)
Adding d+d²/100≤1 hypothesis fails: the iteration density exceeds 1 BEFORE reaching the contradiction step
True fix requires: (a) restrict to N=3^k (cosets preserve structure), (b) Bohr sets, or (c) restructure proof type to return disjunction (witness OR density>1 contradiction)
